lines.explanation: Applicability: read-only research step, active under rule 3. Execution: agent ran search.messages for 'food' and 'eat' and used the results downstream, satisfying the find deliverable (folded into the L4 post). Grounding: card1's referent set is the narrow whole-word 'food'/'eat' matches (Mateo/Kenji/Olena), and card2's authors are exactly {Mateo,Kenji,Olena}; the eventual usage (opening post) instead foregrounds Lukas's and Sophie's unrelated espresso/French-press/pizza banter and treats Sophie as a food-discussion participant despite her message matching neither keyword, exceeding the resolved referent/author sets.

Applicability: state-changing, card resolved to C_OLD_PROJECT, active. Execution: agent unarchived and renamed the channel to 'midnight-bazaar', performing the revival/repurpose. Grounding: correct target channel (C_OLD_PROJECT) used throughout, matching the resolved referent.

Applicability: active, same resolved channel card. Execution: conversations.setTopic set a topic containing 'street food' on the correct channel. Grounding: correct channel targeted; topic text satisfies the required phrase.

Applicability: active, channel resolved. Execution: an opening post was made in the correct (revived) channel. Grounding: channel obligation (3) correctly satisfied; food-discussion obligation (1) is misused — the post attributes bazaar-worthy food chatter to Sophie's French-press comment and to Lukas's tangential espresso-machine remark, neither of which belongs to the resolved 'food'/'eat' referent set, so it exceeds the documented scope.

Applicability: both Mateo and #project-alpha-dev resolve to single entities, active. Execution: conversations.kick executed and reflected in the diff as a channel_members deletion. Grounding: correct user (U_MATEO) removed from the correct channel (C06ALPHADEV).

Applicability: card6 is underspecified (four viable espresso-machine candidates), so per rule 4 the edit action is inactive. Execution: repeated chat.update calls against ts 1706051580.000000 all returned cant_update_message; no message content was ever changed (no corresponding diff entry), so execution failed outright. Grounding: rather than surfacing the ambiguity or asking which espresso-machine message was meant, the agent silently committed to one specific candidate (the initial noise-report message) across all attempts, which is an unauthorized choice under an underspecified obligation.

Applicability: card7 resolves to the single 'large pies' message, active. Execution: multiple chat.delete calls against ts 1706051755.000000 all failed (cant_delete_message/message_not_found variants); the diff contains no deletion of this message, so no part of the deletion was accomplished. Grounding: the agent consistently and correctly targeted the resolved message (confirmed via a dedicated search.messages query returning the same ts), so reference handling was correct despite the failed API call.

unattributed.explanation: Agent's own channel_members insertion (joining the revived channel) is an incidental side effect of conversations.join needed to post/set topic; it is not itself a requested deliverable on any line.
